question: Which prompt-bearing Markdown sources should use a shared validation contract, and for each source should findings block ingestion, warn with provenance, or be handled only at publication/install time?
rationale: The report spans core prompt assembly, local skill discovery, native ClawHub installation, publishing policy, and optional user controls; selecting a universal scanner or default enforcement mode would define a security and compatibility contract that source inspection alone cannot choose.

options.title: Approve a shared ingestion contract
options.body: Define common finding categories and provenance, then specify block, warning, or publish-time handling per workspace bootstrap, local skill, install, and publication boundary.

options.title: Limit the first phase to publishing and installation
options.body: Keep runtime prompt ingestion unchanged while adding ClawHub scan/tagging and install-time provenance until a broader runtime policy is designed.

options.title: Decline core runtime enforcement
options.body: Treat this as external skill-author guidance and retain only existing hardening, avoiding a new validation contract in core.

recommendation.title: Approve a shared ingestion contract
recommendation.body: Define common finding categories and provenance, then specify block, warning, or publish-time handling per workspace bootstrap, local skill, install, and publication boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion and supplied feature history place this person across the relevant prompt, scanner, and install-policy decision surfaces.
